# Notes

<!-- This file is generated by filen-cli. Do not edit it directly! -->

`notes` lists your notes, most recently edited first: when each was last edited (UTC), its
type, its UUID and its title, marked `[archived]` or `[trashed]`. Notes in the trash are left
out unless `--all` is given. With `--json`, the notes are printed as an array of objects with
`uuid`, `title` (`null` when it cannot be decrypted), `type`, `trashed`, `archived`, `pinned`,
`favorited`, `created` and `edited`.

The commands that work on one note (`note-cat`, `note-edit`, `note-rm`) take its exact title or
its UUID. When several notes have that title, they fail and list their UUIDs, so that you can
pass the one you mean.

`note-cat <note>` prints a note's content: a checklist as a Markdown task list, a rich text
note as its HTML, and any other note as it is.

`note-new [title]` creates a note, titled with the current time when no title is given. `--type`
sets its type (`text`, the default, `md`, `code`, `rich` or `checklist`). Its content is read
from `--content-file <file>` (`-` for stdin), or from stdin when stdin is not a terminal; a
checklist's content is a Markdown task list, as `note-edit` takes it. It prints the new note's
UUID (with `--json`, the note as `notes --json` shows it).

`note-rm <note>` moves a note to the trash. `--permanent` deletes it for good instead, after
asking to confirm, which `--yes` answers.

> `notes [OPTIONS]`  
> List your notes, most recently edited first  
> 🠊 `--all` Include the notes in the trash

> `note-cat <NOTE>`  
> Print a note's content  
> 🠊 `<NOTE>` The note's exact title, or its UUID

> `note-new [OPTIONS] [TITLE]`  
> Create a note  
> 🠊 `[TITLE]` The note's title (default: the current time)  
> 🠊 `--type <NOTE_TYPE>` The note's type [default: text] [possible values: text, md, code, rich, checklist]  
> 🠊 `--content-file <FILE>` Read the content from this file, or from stdin for "-" (default: stdin when it is not a terminal, else an empty note)

`note-edit <note>` opens the note's content in an editor and saves it when the editor exits:
the editor `$VISUAL` names, else the one `$EDITOR` names, else `vi` (`notepad` on Windows). The
variable may hold arguments too, such as `code --wait`. A checklist is edited as a Markdown
task list (`- [ ] item`, `- [x] done`), and every other line of it becomes an unchecked item. A
rich text note is edited as its HTML. When the content is unchanged, nothing is saved.

`--content-file <file>` replaces the content with the file's instead, without an editor, and
`--content-file -` with what is read from stdin. Without a terminal, or with `--no-input`,
`note-edit` needs one of them.

Before saving, `note-edit` reads the note again. When it changed while it was being edited, the
edit is not saved: the error names the temporary file the editor's edit is kept in, or the
content file that was not saved. A change made between that check and the save is still
overwritten. When the edit cannot be saved for another reason, such as the note having been
deleted meanwhile or the network failing, the editor's edit is kept in its temporary file too,
and the error names it.

> `note-edit [OPTIONS] <NOTE>`  
> Edit a note's content in an editor ($VISUAL, $EDITOR or vi)  
> 🠊 `<NOTE>` The note's exact title, or its UUID  
> 🠊 `--content-file <FILE>` Replace the content with this file's, or with stdin's for "-", instead of opening an editor

> `note-rm [OPTIONS] <NOTE>`  
> Move a note to the trash, or delete it permanently  
> 🠊 `<NOTE>` The note's exact title, or its UUID  
> 🠊 `--permanent` Delete the note permanently instead (asks to confirm, which --yes answers)

`export-notes <dir>` writes every note to a file in a local directory. A directory that does
not exist yet, or is empty, gets the notes directly (it is created only when there are notes to
export). One that already holds something gets a new `filen-notes-export-<timestamp>`
subdirectory for them, so that no existing file is overwritten.

Notes go into the export directory itself, trashed notes into its `trash/` subdirectory and
archived notes into `archive/`; each subdirectory is created only when a note goes into it. A
file is named after its note's title, with characters a file name cannot hold replaced by `_`,
and a title Windows reserves for a device, such as `CON`, `NUL`, `COM0` or `LPT¹`, also with
spaces after it, prefixed with `_` (a note whose title cannot be decrypted is named
`note-<uuid>`), and `-1`, `-2`, ... appended to tell notes with the same title apart. The
extension follows the note's type: rich text notes are exported as `.html`, Markdown notes and
checklists as `.md` (a checklist as a Markdown task list), and plain text and code notes as
`.txt`.

> `export-notes [PATH]`  
> Export all notes to a local directory
>
> A directory that doesn't exist yet is created, and the notes are exported into it, as they are into an empty directory. A directory that already holds something gets a new `filen-notes-export-<timestamp>` subdirectory for them. Rich text notes are exported as HTML, checklists as Markdown, and trashed and archived notes go into `trash` and `archive` subdirectories.  
> 🠊 `[PATH]` Local directory to export the notes to (default: the current local directory). Used directly when it is missing or empty, otherwise the notes go into a new timestamped subdirectory of it

`import-notes <dir>` creates a note from every `.md`, `.txt` and `.html` file in a local
directory, the reverse of `export-notes`: a note titled after the file's name without its
extension, a Markdown note from a `.md` file, a plain text note from a `.txt` file and a rich
text note from an `.html` file. Other files, hidden files and subdirectories are left out.
The `trash/` and `archive/` subdirectories an export writes are left out too, unless
`--include-trashed` is given: then their notes are imported and moved to the trash or the
archive. A checklist exported as Markdown comes back as a Markdown note, and a code note as a
plain text one. A file that fails is reported, the others are still imported, and the command
then fails.

> `import-notes [OPTIONS] <PATH>`  
> Import the .md, .txt and .html files of a local directory as notes  
> 🠊 `<PATH>` Local directory to import the notes from, such as one export-notes wrote  
> 🠊 `--include-trashed` Also import the notes in its trash/ and archive/ subdirectories, into the trash and the archive
